newsitem.title: USA: Iraq attack sends airline stocks in U.S. into dive.
newsitem.headline: Iraq attack sends airline stocks in U.S. into dive.

text.p: Airline stocks were broadly lower in late-morning trade as oil prices rose after the U.S. missile attack on military targets in southern Iraq.

Among the big losers, Delta Air Lines Inc dropped 2-3/8 to 68-1/2, AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, fell two to 80, United Air's UAL Corp lost 1-7/8 to 46-1/8, Trans World Airlines Inc was off 7/8 to 12-1/2, and Comair Holdings Inc shed 1-1/4 to 22-3/4.
The decline of the airline stocks sent the 20-stock Dow Jones Tranports index down by almost 31 points to 2013.96.

NYMEX crude prices were sharply higher, but off their opening highs, with October crude up $1.15 a barrel to $23.40. In London, prices of IPE Brent crude eased after dealers took profits after a sharp rally, fueled by the U.S. air strikes.

"With the events in the Middle East, oil futures are trading higher, and everyone is expecting higher oil prices," said Frank Calta, director of trading at Anvil Institutional Services. "Who knows how long the conflict will last, and what the response will be from Iraq?"

The U.S. said it launched a cruise missile attack on Iraqi military target in retaliation for a decision by Iraqi president Saddam Hussein to send troops to attack Kurds. Iraq said five people were killed and 19 wounded in the attack on its air defense positions.
Airline stocks were also hit as Merrill Lynch downgraded its near-term rating on British Airways Plc ADRS to neutral from accumulate and its long-term rating to accumulate from buy.

News of a contract agreement between American Air and its pilots did not do much to immediately help AMR stock. "It was overshadowed by Iraq," said Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard A. Rosenblatt & Co Inc. "Everyone was expecting it, so it was not a big deal."
